defects: W6 wave 1 starts in week 21 with no steering meeting reviewing D8 pilot savings (due week 20), and the week 23 check-in that does review D8 decides on wave 2 while wave 1 is already half done and D9 is not yet due.

W6 and W7 give only 4 weeks each to adapt, implement and train across the five remaining plants in two countries, while W5 spends 12 weeks on a single pilot plant, so the rollout is squeezed and the pilot padded.
W5 says the changes launch 'after the readiness workshop', but Workshop 2 (week 17) decides the wave composition, so no meeting actually approves the pilot go-live.
W1 allows only 2 weeks (D1 due week 2) to build baselines, observe lines and trace loss causes in two plants, which is too short for a floor diagnostic.
The notes to the partner cite 6-week waves while W6 and W7 run 4 weeks each, so the stated sizing logic contradicts the plan.

D10 final readout pack is due week 28, but wave 2 plants only go live by week 26 (D13) and no deliverable reports wave 2 cost per part against baseline, so the final readout cannot show the 'every plant' success criterion.
W4 sizing by plant starts in week 4, before the D2 and D3 baselines for four of the six plants (due week 5) exist and before Workshop 1 reviews them.
No meeting or deliverable decides which plants form wave 1 and wave 2, and the week 19 check-in, held as W7 wave 1 starts, decides how wave 2 is measured rather than whether wave 1 starts.
D11 (wave 1 training and go-live record for each plant) is due week 20, one week after W7 starts, which is too little time to adapt, train and go live in several plants.
Workshop 3 (week 23) re-reviews D7, D8 and D9, which the week 19 check-in already covered, and its stated purpose ('before final readout') does not match its decision (wave 2 go/no-go).

why: Y gates the pilot go-live and wave 2 on the evidence produced just before each meeting, and gives the diagnostic and rollout waves more realistic durations; X starts wave 1 with no steering review of the pilot savings and squeezes five plants into two 4-week waves. Y's main weakness is that wave 2 plants have only about two weeks of cost data before the final readout, and adding a few weeks at the end fixes that; X would need its rollout timing and its gates reworked.
